purpose: Operational vocabulary for play recognition. These are observable heuristics for tracking/video, not rulebook terms. IDs are stable; add a new ID rather than changing the meaning of an old one.

play_types.name: Isolation
play_types.definition: One ball handler attacks a set defender while four teammates stay spaced; no screen creates the advantage.
signals: one defender within 6 ft of the handler
four teammates outside 12 ft of the handler
no on-ball screen in the 1.5 s before the drive

play_types.name: Transition
play_types.definition: The offense attacks before the defense is set, usually within 6 s of a possession change.
signals: possession change within the last 6 s
ball advanced past half court before the defense is set

play_types.name: Pick-and-roll — ball handler
play_types.definition: An on-ball screen is set and the handler uses it to create a drive, pass, or shot.
signals: screener stationary next to the handler's defender
handler dribbles toward or away from the screen
handler decision within 2 s of the screen

play_types.name: Pick-and-roll — roll man
play_types.definition: The screener dives to the rim or pops to the perimeter and becomes the receiver or finisher.
signals: screener moves toward the rim or pops after contact
screener receives the ball or creates a shot
handler and screener remain within a passing lane

play_types.name: Post-up
play_types.definition: A player catches with their back to the basket inside roughly 12 ft and attacks from the post.
signals: catch inside 12 ft with back to basket
dribble or pivot toward the rim

play_types.name: Spot-up
play_types.definition: A stationary catch outside roughly 15 ft, followed by a shot or a closeout attack.
signals: catch with feet set outside 15 ft

play_types.name: Dribble handoff
play_types.definition: A ball handler hands the ball to a teammate in motion, often used as a screen-like action.
signals: ball transfers hand-to-hand near the handler
receiver continues into a drive or shot

play_types.name: Cut
play_types.definition: An off-ball player moves toward the rim or open space to receive a pass.
signals: off-ball player accelerates toward the rim or gap
defender trailing or losing the player
pass arrives within 1 s of the move

play_types.name: Off-ball screen
play_types.definition: A player runs off a screen away from the ball to get open.
signals: stationary screener away from the ball
cutter changes direction around the screen

play_types.name: Putback
play_types.definition: An offensive rebound is immediately followed by a shot attempt.
signals: shot attempt within 1.5 s of the rebound

play_types.name: Miscellaneous
play_types.definition: A possession that does not fit the other play types; broken plays are a real category.
signals: no play type passes its confidence threshold
loose ball, deflection, or broken action

coverages.name: Man-to-man
coverages.definition: Each defender is primarily responsible for one offensive player.
signals: tight assignment stability across the possession

coverages.name: Drop coverage
coverages.definition: The screener's defender stays below the screen level, between the roller and the rim.

coverages.name: Switch
coverages.definition: Two defenders exchange assignments after a screen.

coverages.name: Hedge / show
coverages.definition: The screener's defender jumps above the screen level to slow the handler, then recovers.

coverages.name: Ice / down
coverages.definition: The handler's defender forces the ball toward the baseline while the screener's defender stays high.
signals: handler forced to the baseline side
help rotates from the weak side

coverages.name: Trap / blitz
coverages.definition: Two defenders aggressively double the ball handler.
signals: two defenders within 6 ft of the handler
short roll or skip pass available

coverages.name: 2-3 zone
coverages.definition: Two defenders high and three low, guarding space rather than specific players.

coverages.name: 3-2 zone
coverages.definition: Three defenders high and two low.

coverages.name: 1-3-1 zone
coverages.definition: One point defender, three across the wing area, one on the baseline.

coverages.name: Full-court press
coverages.definition: The defense picks up above half court, often after a made basket or inbound.
signals: defenders above half court at inbound

play_families.name: Horns
play_families.definition: Two bigs at the elbows with guards in the corners; a base for PnR, handoff, and pinch actions.

play_families.name: Spain PnR
play_families.definition: A back screen for the screener precedes the ball screen, creating a second defender decision.
signals: back screen before the ball screen
handler rejects or uses the screen

play_families.name: Zoom
play_families.definition: A dribble handoff into a ball-screen-like action, often with a re-screen.
signals: defense forced into a second decision

play_families.name: Floppy
play_families.definition: A shooter chooses between two off-ball screens on opposite sides.
signals: two screeners set for one shooter

play_families.name: Elevator
play_families.definition: Two players form a gate and close it behind a shooter cutting through.

play_families.name: Stagger
play_families.definition: Two sequential screens for the same cutter.

play_families.name: Triangle
play_families.definition: Sideline triangle with a weak-side two-man game; a read-and-react system rather than a set play.

notes: Play types follow the NBA/Synergy vocabulary; coverage and family labels are orthogonal.
A possession can have multiple labels; do not force a single class.
Definitions are heuristics for tracking/video, not official rulebook terms.
